title: SDSS DR18 galaxy redshifts in a 120 to 240 degree strip at declination 0 to 0.5 degrees (a wedge)

object.name: The SDSS Legacy main galaxy sample in a thin equatorial strip
object.frame: ICRS, J2000: right ascension 120 to 240 degrees, declination 0 to 0.5 degrees

facility.observatory: Sloan Digital Sky Survey (Apache Point 2.5 m)

credit: SDSS-I/II (the Legacy main sample), Data Release 18: Almeida et al. 2023, ApJS 267, 44; Strauss et al. 2002, AJ 124, 1810

license.statement: SDSS states that all data released in its public data releases are considered public domain (image-use policy, read 2026-10-09); it asks for the acknowledgement of the survey phase and the data release.

columns.name: right ascension
columns.description: J2000, rounded to 1e-4 degree (0.36 arcsecond step, 0.18 arcsecond largest rounding)

columns.name: redshift
columns.description: the spectroscopic redshift, its eight digits kept

masks.rule: class GALAXY, zWarning 0, the survey's primary spectrum
r < 17.77, the Legacy main sample limit
z up to 0.12, declination 0 to 0.5 degrees: the first cut of six declared before the run that fits the size ceilings

reductions: The strip declination 0 to 0.5 degrees, right ascension 120 to 240 degrees and redshift up to 0.12: 2911 of the 16247 galaxies the query returned, sorted by right ascension.

Right ascension is rounded to 1e-4 degree (a stated step, largest rounding 0.18 arcsecond); the redshift keeps its eight digits. Declination, magnitudes, errors and identifiers are not kept: the strip is thin, and declination is its limits.
This is a flux-limited sample (r < 17.77, fiber-limited, with fiber collisions): it thins with distance because fainter galaxies fall below the limit. A page that draws it must say so.

source.archive: SDSS Data Release 18, SkyServer SQL search

citations.text: Almeida et al. 2023, ApJS 267, 44 (The Eighteenth Data Release of the Sloan Digital Sky Surveys)
Strauss et al. 2002, AJ 124, 1810 (Spectroscopic target selection in the SDSS: the main galaxy sample)

options.query:
SELECT specObjID, ra, dec, z, zErr, petroMag_r
FROM SpecPhoto
WHERE class='GALAXY' AND zWarning=0 AND survey='sdss' AND sciencePrimary=1
  AND petroMag_r<17.77 AND dec BETWEEN 0 AND 2 AND ra BETWEEN 120 AND 240
  AND z BETWEEN 0.01 AND 0.2
ORDER BY specObjID

steps: Read ra, dec and z from the SkyServer answer to the query in options.query.
Sort by right ascension, then redshift.
Store right ascension and redshift as table-columns/1.

assumptions: The redshift is the survey pipeline's (zWarning 0), heliocentric: it includes the galaxy's peculiar velocity, which the "fingers of God" in a wedge diagram show.
A wedge needs a distance: the page converts redshift with a stated cosmology (flat, Omega_m 0.3, H0 70 in the lessons).

validation.check: galaxies in the strip are clustered: counts in 5-degree sectors of 25 Mpc shells (100 to 400 Mpc) have a variance-to-mean ratio above 2 (Poisson would give 1)

against.quantity: variance-to-mean ratio of counts in cells
